exact_statement: Prove a parameterized support-minimal unequal-cardinality equal-product path relation that avoids every prescribed prime below N^(1/2-epsilon) while remaining in a multiplicative tail of width depending only on epsilon, and determine whether it rules out deterministic and randomized per-integer deletion classifiers implemented by adaptive prime-valuation decision trees whose all-zero branch has positive-density input. Any randomized theorem must give an explicit success-probability bound from expected deletion cost. It must not claim a result for global alteration, arbitrary exact-label rules, the full transversal number, or Erdos 786.
scope_notes: Variant lock: relations use two disjoint Finsets of distinct positive integers with equal products and unequal cardinalities; cancelled coefficients are in {-1,0,1}.
The predecessor U.1--U.3 campaign is frozen at independent_audit and is a read-only dependency. This successor may strengthen its geometric parameter range but may not alter its evidence.

A deterministic classifier applies one finite rooted decision tree to every integer above a declared lower threshold. An internal node may query the exact valuation nu_p(n), and the next query may depend on previous answers. The all-zero branch must terminate.

A randomized classifier first draws a shared seed and then applies the corresponding deterministic tree to every integer. Off-zero branches and their queried primes are unrestricted; only the all-zero branch is constrained.

The model excludes a different hard-coded tree for every integer, exact integer-label queries, decisions using previously classified integers, global repair/alteration, and a post hoc choice of the tree after seeing the adversarial relation.
The geometric theorem may use a sequence epsilon_K only with epsilon_K^2 K tending to infinity. A fixed epsilon gives a fixed multiplicative tail and controlled primes up to N^(1/2-epsilon).
A randomized no-go conclusion must be quantitative: the probability of returning a transversal is bounded in terms of expected deletion cost and the population of the all-zero branch.
No conclusion about tau(H_N), an o(N) transversal, the infinite density problem, or Erdos 786 is permitted.
Public search for an exact solution of Erdos 786 remains prohibited. Ordinary named background such as Bertrand's postulate and elementary union/expectation bounds is allowed.

variant_lock.relation: disjoint finite shores with equal products and unequal cardinalities
variant_lock.minimality: no proper nonempty signed subrelation on the displayed support
variant_lock.forbidden: multisets, repetitions, approximate identities, or arbitrary integer coefficients

frozen_geometric_target.parameters: N=b^K, 0<epsilon_K<1/2, u_K=floor((1/2-epsilon_K)K), s_K=floor(epsilon_K K/4), epsilon_K^2 K -> infinity
frozen_geometric_target.controlled_primes: every prescribed prime is different from b and smaller than b^u_K
frozen_geometric_target.tail: all relation vertices exceed N/b^(D_K+1), where D_K=ceil(8/epsilon_K+1)
frozen_geometric_target.support: 2s_K+1 distinct vertices with ordered path prime incidence outside b

frozen_query_model.tree: one finite exact-prime-valuation decision tree per K and random seed, applied uniformly to all n above t_K
frozen_query_model.zero_branch: P_(K,omega) is the set of primes queried after repeated valuation-zero answers; b is absent, max P<b^u_K, and sum_(p in P)1/p<=1-delta
frozen_query_model.target_bound: Pr(D_(K,omega) is a transversal of H_N)<=mu_K/(delta N-t_K) whenever the denominator is positive

read_only_dependency.result: U.1--U.3 constant-width path and static valuation-cylinder obstruction
